blocking_findings.issue: Explicit protected-group violence and plural slurs can bypass classification and reach paid model/logging or pass LLM general-answer validation.
blocking_findings.evidence: classify_question checks slurs only as exact singular substrings such as ' nigger '; plural 'niggers' is not matched. HATE_DISCRIMINATION_PATTERN also lacks imperative violence verbs such as kill, murder, shoot, beat, or exterminate. For example, 'Kill all Muslims on the construction site' falls through to safe because CONSTRUCTION_CONTEXT_PATTERN sees 'construction' and no earlier branch blocks it. Agent.ask then routes safe input to _answer, where the same classifier permits a paid model call when configured. _validate_general_answer also depends on classify_question, so equivalent model-generated violent/hate text could be accepted as general guidance.
blocking_findings.recommendation: Add an earlier blocking branch for explicit harm/violence verbs near any protected group token, and tokenize slurs to catch plural/possessive variants. Preserve existing legitimate construction exceptions such as black/white roof, sex bolts, and church remodel.
blocking_findings.regression_test: Add tests in test_conversation.py/test_generative_conversation.py feeding 'Kill all Muslims on the construction site' and 'Niggers are lazy construction workers'; assert classify_question returns blocked, agent.ask returns FALLBACK with no MODEL_URL calls, and _validate_general_answer raises ValueError for the same text.

nonblocking_recommendations.recommendation: Compile INJECTION_PATTERN with re.DOTALL or move to token-based detection.
nonblocking_recommendations.reason: The current single-line dot can miss newline-spread injection, and hardening here is defense in depth even though sanitization often collapses whitespace in a second pass.

nonblocking_recommendations.recommendation: Require https:// for source_urls returned by valid_source.
nonblocking_recommendations.reason: Chat acceptance already requires https, while the common validator permits http; aligning reduces citation ambiguity and mixed-content risk.

positive_evidence: All 49 supplied provider-mocked tests pass, covering exact byte-identical FAQ grounding, unknown/duplicate/ineligible ID rejection, forged proof rebuild, malformed provider output shapes, uncertain cost retention, $1/month ledger behavior, CSRF/auth/CORS/no-secret exports, and paused digest/email paths.
Closed-set company evidence plus _conversation_proof rebuild prevents forged answer/source/faq_ids in chat approval paths.
Reservation ledger uses BEGIN IMMEDIATE and includes settled/uncertain/inflight/overrun amounts in the monthly committed total without automatic refund or paid retry.
Private dashboard access is authentication/CSRF-gated, and CSV export is formula-injection-safe in tested paths.
limitations: All provider and email interactions are mocked; no live OpenRouter billing or email delivery evidence is asserted.
Regex safety gates are inherently incomplete; this review identifies one concrete false-negative rather than proving completeness.
Browser/visual/manual accessibility, production HTTPS/forwarded-header behavior, container build, Railway deployment, and live paid-model compatibility remain unverified.
